editorial:
Imagine waking up after a few too many pints of Guinness in Dublin, only to realize you are no longer a human. You are now a small, scurrying rat. That is exactly what happens to our main guy, a regular working-class dad who just wanted a quiet night out. The vibe is a wild mix of funny and sad, as you watch him try to navigate his own house and communicate with his family while being small enough to fit in a shoe. It feels like a strange dream, but the heart of the story is really about how he sees his family differently now that he is literally at their feet.

The acting is great, especially seeing the lead actor play a rodent through voice and movement. The pacing is quick, though some of the slower family scenes might feel a bit long. If you love stories about people learning life lessons the hard way, you will dig this.
endingExplained: At the very end, the main character finally learns to be honest and kind to his family. After a scary close call with a house cat, he makes a heartfelt apology for his past mistakes. This emotional breakthrough breaks the spell. He wakes up back in his human body in his own bed. He hugs his kids and wife, promising to be a better man, and the movie ends with him throwing away his drinking habits for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird stories with a big heart.
